```{r}
#Part A

#Question A1A
shoe_size <- c(6.5, 9.0, 8.5, 8.5, 10.5, 7.0, 9.5, 9.0, 13.0, 7.5,
               10.5, 8.5, 12.0, 10.5, 13.0, 11.5, 8.5, 5.0, 10.0, 6.5,
               7.5, 8.5, 10.5, 8.5, 10.5, 11.0, 9.0, 13.0)

height <- c(66.0, 68.0, 64.5, 65.0, 70.0, 64.0, 70.0, 71.0, 72.0, 64.0,
            74.5, 67.0, 71.0, 71.0, 77.0, 72.0, 59.0, 62.0, 72.0, 66.0,
            64.0, 67.0, 73.0, 69.0, 72.0, 70.0, 69.0, 70.0)

gender <- c("F", "F", "F", "F", "M", "F", "F", "M", "M", "F",
            "M", "F", "M", "M", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F",
            "F", "M", "M", "F", "M", "M", "M", "M")

shoesize <- data.frame(shoe_size, height, gender)

write.csv(shoesize, "shoesize.csv", row.names = FALSE)

shoesize

#Question A1B
shoesize <- read.csv("shoesize.csv")

tail(shoesize, 5)

#Question A1C
str(shoesize)

#Question A1D
dim(shoesize)
nrow(shoesize)
ncol(shoesize)

#Question A1E
summary(shoesize)
#str() tells you what the data looks like, while summary() tells you what the data contains statistically.

#Question A1F
males   <- shoesize[shoesize$gender == "M", ]
females <- shoesize[shoesize$gender == "F", ]

males
females

#Question A1G
mean(shoesize$shoe_size)
mean(shoesize$height)

#Question A1H
cor(shoesize$shoe_size, shoesize$height)
#Yes, there is a moderate to strong positive relationship. A correlation of 0.66 indicates that as shoe size increases, height tends to increase as well.

#Question A2
shoesize$gender <- factor(shoesize$gender)

levels(shoesize$gender)
shoesize$gender

#Question A3
#Because the .Rmd file and its data files (like shoesize.csv) are stored together in the same folder. When R Markdown knits, it sets that folder as the working directory automatically, so read.csv("shoesize.csv") always works regardless of what folder the user’s R console was pointing to.

#Question A4
str(shoesize)
#gender is now correctly a Factor, and shoe_size and height are numeric, which is expected. However, if a column like shoe_size were accidentally imported as character (e.g., due to a stray value like "8.5a" in the original file), any numeric operation: mean(), cor(), order(), would throw an error.

#Question A5
#head() only shows the first 6 rows, so problems at the bottom of the file go completely unnoticed. Common issues that head() alone would miss include: trailing empty rows, repeated headers at the end, corrupted last entries, or import cutoffs where the file didn’t fully load.

#Question A6A
cor(shoesize$shoe_size, shoesize$height)

#Question A6B
shoesize[shoesize$shoe_size >= 11, ]

#Question A7
# Mean height by gender
mean(males$height)
mean(females$height)

# Mean shoe size by gender
mean(males$shoe_size)
mean(females$shoe_size)

#Yes. The overall correlation of 0.66 is partly driven by gender acting as a grouping factor; males cluster at high shoe size + high height, females at low shoe size + low height.
```
